name: Tapajó
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, unclassifiable, essentially unattested; Glottolog lists no descriptive references

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and JSON for tapa1261 (Hammarström et al.), and reference record 683601
sources.note: Classification 'Unclassifiable', status extinct; the sole reference is Nimuendajú 1949 typed a wordlist or less. No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) source exists.
Secondary; repeats Nimuendajú: only three words/names survive (Tapajó, Orucurá, Aura); language used for catechism in the 1660s; unclassified. No stress information.

sources.citation: Bettendorff, João Filipe. [1698] 2010. Crônica da Missão dos Padres da Companhia de Jesus no Estado do Maranhão. Brasília: Edições do Senado Federal, vol. 115. Capítulo 'Breve relação do que obrei pelos Tapajós'. (Nimuendajú cites the 1910 RIHGB 72 edition, p. 168.)
sources.note: Nothing. Reports only that in 1661 the author had catechisms made 'em língua dos tapajós, outro os urucucus' translated from the Lingua Geral; the catechism itself is lost. No words of the language are given.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1952. The Tapajó. Translated and edited by John Howland Rowe. Kroeber Anthropological Society Papers 6: 1-25.
sources.note: Nothing. 'Language' paragraph p. 5 is the English of the 1949 text: 'Of the Tapajó language we know only three proper names.. None of these can be interpreted in Tupi.' Rowe's note 3 (p. 12) adds Barata 1950b's point that Bettendorff's seven native words attributed to the Tapajó are all good Tupi (Lingua Geral), i.e. not Tapajó data.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1949. Os Tapajó. Boletim do Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi 10: 93-106. (Glottolog ref 683601 = hh:e:Nimuendaju:Tapajo:1949, listed by Glottolog as a wordlist or less; the only Glottolog reference for tapa1261)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'LÍNGUA' section (pp. 97-98) states that neither tribe at the mouth of the Tapajós spoke Tupi and that of the Tapajó language only three proper names are known (tribe name, chief Orucurá, 'devil' Aura, from Heriarte p. 36); no wordlist, no phonological data, no mention of accent.
sources.venue: Boletim do Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi

sources.citation: Heriarte, Mauricio de. 1874 [ms. 1662]. Descripção do Estado do Maranhão, Pará, Corupá e Rio das Amazonas. Vienna: Imprensa do filho de Carlos Gerold. 'Provincia dos Tapajos', §35-36, pp. 35-37.
sources.note: Nothing. This is the primary 17th-century source of the only Tapajó word: 'he Potaba de Aura, que, na sua lingoa, he o nome do diabo' (p. 36); also says the Indians of the river other than the Tupinambaranas 'fallam differentes lingoas' (p. 40). No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Standard classificatory listing likely noting Tapajó among languages known only from names; would confirm no lexical data exist.

sources.citation: Barata, Frederico. 1950b. [Review/note on Nimuendajú 1949 'Os Tapajó', discussing the linguistic evidence; cited by Rowe in Nimuendajú 1952, note 3]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other discussion of the Tapajó linguistic evidence; per Rowe it shows Bettendorff's seven 'Tapajó' words are all Lingua Geral. Could only confirm the absence of data, not supply a stress statement.
